Subject: Storacorp marketplace bespoke ask - rev-share transition + accelerated credit (requesting exec ok)

Hi Karthik / Marissa —

Quick summary: Storacorp (large enterprise org) is asking for a tailored Marketplace private-offer on AWS to support a platform migration. They want: a) an initial blended rev-share that favors Storacorp for the first 6 months (60/40 to partner), then reverts to standard 80/20 Redwood/AWS split; b) an upfront onboarding credit (accelerated bill credit) applied across first two invoices; and c) net60 billing for the first 3 months while they finalize procurement.

Why this is urgent: they gave a migration window targeting production traffic in July; delaying approval will push their go-live and risk losing the multiyear subscription. The ARR is ~$1.9M first-year run-rate.

Attachments: Storacorp_SOW_v1.pdf, Revshare_impact_model.xlsx (simple impact calc).

Ask: Can Deal Desk escalate for an executive exception? The combined rev-share deviation + billing terms exceed our standard delegated approval. Recommend time-boxed concession (90 days) and a formal onboarding milestone.

Notes: I validated with Product that technical compatibility is good; Legal flagged a need for an explicit transition period clause if we change rev-share buckets.

Thanks — any questions, I'm available on phone.

—Vanessa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Storacorp marketplace bespoke ask - rev-share transition + accelerated credit (requesting exec ok)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. Quick read-through notes:
- ARR and runway look real; this is a material size for marketplace revenue and impacts upfront recognition.
- The requested initial 60/40 split to the customer for 6 months then revert is outside our standard carves. Typically exceptions beyond 3 months require Marissa-level sign-off because it materially changes forecast and partner commissions.
- Net60 for three months + an onboarding bill credit increases cash risk and requires Finance alignment.

Given the combination of nonstandard rev-share duration + billing mechanics, I think we should escalate to Marissa for exec exception. I ran a quick delta model — see Revshare_impact_model.xlsx — shows ~12% reduction in Redwood recognized revenue in Q3 if approved.

Recommendation for a conservative, approvable concession:
1) Approve a time-limited transitional split: 50/50 for first 90 days (instead of 60/40 for 6 months).
2) Onboarding credit capped to $60k applied as a credit on invoice 1 and 2 only.
3) Net60 for first two invoices only (not three).
4) Require clause that reverts to standard marketplace rev-share and billing after 90 days; failure to hit onboarding milestones voids the concession.

If Marissa agrees I will route to Legal for precise language and Finance for the billing flow.

Karthik
Deal Desk Lead

Thanks Karthik / Vanessa. I reviewed the impact model and the contextual rationale. Approve with conditions:

1) Approve a 50/50 transitional rev-share for the first 90 days only (not 6 months).
2) Approve onboarding credit up to $60k applied to invoice 1 & 2.
3) Approve Net60 for invoice 1 & 2 only. Subsequent invoices on standard net30.
4) Legal must include a transition clause that reverts rev-share to standard marketplace terms after 90 days and ties the concession to concrete onboarding milestones (activation of X product lines + ingestion of 5TB data).
5) Finance to confirm that the onboarding credit will be treated as an invoice-level credit and not a modification to recognized revenue; notify Accounting.
6) Exception approval is valid only if AWS Marketplace confirms technical routing and there is an explicit Marketplace acceptance sign-off (ticket or email) — Karthik to coordinate with AWS contact.

If Legal/Finance/AWS confirm the mechanism, we can proceed. Karthik — please route to Legal and Finance and come back to me with the final language by EOD tomorrow.

Marissa
